IPL 2026 — Data Visualization¶

Objective¶

Transform the cleaned IPL 2026 dataset into clear, informative, and visually appealing charts.

Tools¶

  • Python
  • Pandas
  • NumPy
  • Matplotlib
  • Seaborn

Visualization Theme¶

  • Primary: IPL Blue (#1E3A8A)
  • Secondary: Trophy Gold (#D4A017)
  • Accent: Cricket Red (#D62828)
  • Background: Light (#F4F6FA)

Workflow¶

  1. Load and inspect the integrated dataset.
  2. Configure the IPL-inspired chart theme.
  3. Visualize match scoring patterns.
  4. Compare team and player performance.
  5. Analyze venue and innings trends.
  6. Save selected charts for the project report.
In [1]:
# Data manipulation
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Visualization
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# File handling
from pathlib import Path

# IPL-inspired color palette
IPL_BLUE = "#1E3A8A"
TROPHY_GOLD = "#D4A017"
CRICKET_RED = "#D62828"
PITCH_GREEN = "#2E7D32"
LIGHT_BG = "#F4F6FA"

# Configure visualization style
sns.set_theme(
    style="whitegrid",
    context="notebook",
    font_scale=1.1
)

plt.rcParams["figure.figsize"] = (10, 6)
plt.rcParams["figure.facecolor"] = LIGHT_BG
plt.rcParams["axes.facecolor"] = LIGHT_BG
plt.rcParams["axes.edgecolor"] = IPL_BLUE
plt.rcParams["axes.labelcolor"] = IPL_BLUE
plt.rcParams["axes.titlecolor"] = IPL_BLUE
plt.rcParams["xtick.color"] = IPL_BLUE
plt.rcParams["ytick.color"] = IPL_BLUE
plt.rcParams["grid.color"] = "#D9DEE8"
plt.rcParams["grid.alpha"] = 0.7
plt.rcParams["savefig.dpi"] = 300
plt.rcParams["savefig.bbox"] = "tight"

print("Libraries imported and IPL theme configured.")

Libraries imported and IPL theme configured.

Step 2: Load the Integrated IPL Dataset¶

In this step, we will load the cleaned and integrated IPL 2026 dataset created during the data integration phase.

We will:

  • Load the CSV file using Pandas.
  • Check the dataset's dimensions and column names.
  • Inspect the first few rows and data types.
  • Confirm that the dataset is ready for visualization.
In [2]:

print("\nData Types:")

Step 3: Create Match-Level Data¶

The integrated dataset contains ball-by-ball records. For match-level visualizations, we need to aggregate these records so each match is represented once.

In this step, we will:

  • Group deliveries by match number.
  • Calculate total runs scored in each match.
  • Count the number of innings recorded.
  • Keep the venue and participating teams for later analysis.

This aggregated dataset will help us visualize match totals and compare scoring patterns across venues.

In [3]:
# Create match-level summary

match_summary = (
    df.groupby("match_no")
    .agg(
        total_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        total_extras=("extras", "sum"),
        innings_count=("innings", "nunique"),
        venue=("venue_delivery", "first"),
        teams=("batting_team", lambda x: " vs ".join(sorted(x.dropna().unique())))
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Calculate total match runs
match_summary["match_total"] = (
    match_summary["total_runs"] + match_summary["total_extras"]
)

# Inspect the summary
print("Match-level dataset shape:", match_summary.shape)
display(match_summary.head(10))

print("\nMatch count:", match_summary["match_no"].nunique())
print("Missing match totals:", match_summary["match_total"].isna().sum())

Step 4: Match-Wise Total Runs¶

A bar chart helps us compare total runs scored across matches and identify high-scoring and low-scoring games.

We will:

  • Plot match number on the X-axis.
  • Plot total match runs on the Y-axis.
  • Use the IPL blue and gold theme.
  • Highlight the match with the highest recorded total.

This visualization gives us an overview of scoring variation across the recorded matches.

In [4]:
# Match-wise total runs visualization

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Find the highest-scoring match
highest_match = match_summary.loc[
    match_summary["match_total"].idxmax()
]

# Create the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 6))

bars = plt.bar(
    match_summary["match_no"],
    match_summary["match_total"],
    color=IPL_BLUE,
    edgecolor="white"
)

# Highlight the highest-scoring match
bars[highest_match.name].set_color(TROPHY_GOLD)

plt.title(
    "Total Runs Scored in Each IPL 2026 Match",
    fontsize=16,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Match Number", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Total Runs", fontsize=12)

plt.xticks(match_summary["match_no"], rotation=90)
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print(
    f"Highest recorded total: {highest_match['match_total']} runs "
    f"(Match {int(highest_match['match_no'])})"
)

Highest recorded total: 528 runs (Match 35)

Step 5: Distribution of Total Runs¶

A histogram helps us understand how frequently different match-total ranges occur.

We will:

  • Divide match totals into score ranges (bins).
  • Count how many matches fall into each range.
  • Add a vertical line for the average match total.
  • Use the IPL blue and gold color palette.

This visualization helps identify the most common scoring ranges and whether the distribution is concentrated or spread out.

In [5]:
# Distribution of total runs across matches

average_total = match_summary["match_total"].mean()

plt.figure(figsize=(11, 6))

plt.hist(
    match_summary["match_total"],
    bins=12,
    color=IPL_BLUE,
    edgecolor="white",
    alpha=0.9
)

plt.axvline(
    average_total,
    color=TROPHY_GOLD,
    linestyle="--",
    linewidth=2.5,
    label=f"Average: {average_total:.1f} runs"
)

plt.title(
    "Distribution of Total Runs Across IPL 2026 Matches",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Total Runs in a Match", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Number of Matches", fontsize=12)
plt.legend()
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print(f"Average match total: {average_total:.2f}")
print(f"Median match total: {match_summary['match_total'].median():.2f}")

Step 6: Average Match Total by Venue¶

Different venues may show different scoring patterns. In this step, we will calculate the average total runs recorded per match at each venue.

We will:

  • Group matches by venue.
  • Calculate the average match total and number of matches at each venue.
  • Sort venues by average total.
  • Visualize the comparison with a horizontal bar chart.

We will also display the number of matches alongside each venue, since averages based on a small number of matches should be interpreted cautiously.

In [6]:
# Average match total by venue

venue_summary = (
    match_summary.groupby("venue")
    .agg(
        average_total=("match_total", "mean"),
        matches=("match_no", "nunique")
    )
    .sort_values("average_total")
    .reset_index()
)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

bars = plt.barh(
    venue_summary["venue"],
    venue_summary["average_total"],
    color=IPL_BLUE,
    edgecolor="white"
)

# Highlight the venue with the highest average
bars[-1].set_color(TROPHY_GOLD)

plt.title(
    "Average Match Total by Venue — IPL 2026",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Average Total Runs", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Venue", fontsize=12)

# Add match counts to the labels
venue_labels = [
    f"{venue} (n={count})"
    for venue, count in zip(
        venue_summary["venue"],
        venue_summary["matches"]
    )
]
plt.yticks(range(len(venue_labels)), venue_labels)

plt.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

display(venue_summary.round(2))

Step 7: First-Innings vs Second-Innings Scores¶

A box plot summarizes the distribution of scores and helps compare the center, spread, and potential outliers of two groups.

In this step, we will:

  • Calculate the total runs for each match innings.
  • Separate first-innings and second-innings scores.
  • Exclude innings beyond the first two, such as Super Overs.
  • Compare the score distributions with a box plot.

We will retain the abandoned match for now but identify its incomplete innings before interpreting the chart.

In [7]:
# Calculate innings-level scores

innings_summary = (
    df[df["innings"].isin([1, 2])]
    .groupby(["match_no", "innings"])
    .agg(
        innings_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        extras=("extras", "sum")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

innings_summary["total_score"] = (
    innings_summary["innings_runs"] + innings_summary["extras"]
)

# Separate first and second innings
first_innings = innings_summary.loc[
    innings_summary["innings"] == 1, "total_score"
]

second_innings = innings_summary.loc[
    innings_summary["innings"] == 2, "total_score"
]

# Create box plot
plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))

box = plt.boxplot(
    [first_innings, second_innings],
    tick_labels=["First Innings", "Second Innings"],
    patch_artist=True,
    medianprops={"color": TROPHY_GOLD, "linewidth": 2}
)

box["boxes"][0].set_facecolor(IPL_BLUE)
box["boxes"][1].set_facecolor(PITCH_GREEN)

plt.title(
    "First-Innings vs Second-Innings Scores",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.ylabel("Total Runs", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("First innings:")
print(first_innings.describe().round(2))

print("\nSecond innings:")
print(second_innings.describe().round(2))

Step 8: Innings Score Comparison — Completed Matches¶

The previous box plot included an incomplete match. To make the comparison more representative, we will filter the data to matches with at least two recorded innings.

We will:

  • Identify matches with two or more recorded innings.
  • Filter the innings-level summary to those matches.
  • Compare first- and second-innings scores using a box plot.
  • Print the sample sizes and average scores for both innings.

This removes the abandoned match's unusually low first-innings score from the comparison.

In [8]:
# Filter to matches with at least two recorded innings

completed_match_ids = match_summary.loc[
    match_summary["innings_count"] >= 2, "match_no"
]

completed_innings = innings_summary[
    innings_summary["match_no"].isin(completed_match_ids)
]

first_completed = completed_innings.loc[
    completed_innings["innings"] == 1, "total_score"
]

second_completed = completed_innings.loc[
    completed_innings["innings"] == 2, "total_score"
]

# Plot comparison
plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))

box = plt.boxplot(
    [first_completed, second_completed],
    tick_labels=["First Innings", "Second Innings"],
    patch_artist=True,
    medianprops={"color": TROPHY_GOLD, "linewidth": 2}
)

box["boxes"][0].set_facecolor(IPL_BLUE)
box["boxes"][1].set_facecolor(PITCH_GREEN)

plt.title(
    "Innings Scores in Matches with Two Recorded Innings",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.ylabel("Total Runs", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("First innings — count:", len(first_completed))
print("First innings — mean:", round(first_completed.mean(), 2))
print("First innings — median:", round(first_completed.median(), 2))

print("\nSecond innings — count:", len(second_completed))
print("Second innings — mean:", round(second_completed.mean(), 2))
print("Second innings — median:", round(second_completed.median(), 2))

Step 9: Top 10 Run Scorers — IPL 2026¶

A horizontal bar chart is useful for comparing player performance and ranking the leading run scorers.

We will:

  • Group deliveries by striker.
  • Sum runs scored off the bat for each player.
  • Select the top 10 batters.
  • Plot their runs in descending order.

This visualization focuses on runs scored from the bat, excluding extras.

In [9]:
# Calculate top 10 run scorers

batter_summary = (
    df.groupby("striker")
    .agg(
        total_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        balls_recorded=("over", "count")
    )
    .sort_values("total_runs", ascending=False)
    .head(10)
    .sort_values("total_runs")
    .reset_index()
)

plt.figure(figsize=(11, 7))

bars = plt.barh(
    batter_summary["striker"],
    batter_summary["total_runs"],
    color=IPL_BLUE,
    edgecolor="white"
)

# Highlight the top scorer
bars[-1].set_color(TROPHY_GOLD)

plt.title(
    "Top 10 Run Scorers — IPL 2026",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Runs Scored off the Bat", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Batter", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Step 10: Strike Rate of the Top 10 Run Scorers¶

Runs scored show a batter's total contribution, while strike rate measures scoring speed.

Formula:

Strike Rate = (Runs Scored ÷ Balls Faced) × 100

In this step, we will:

  • Calculate valid balls faced for each batter by excluding wides.
  • Calculate each batter's strike rate.
  • Compare the top 10 run scorers from Step 9.
  • Use a horizontal bar chart to compare scoring speed.

Strike rate should be interpreted alongside total runs, since a high strike rate over a small number of balls may not represent the same contribution as a high run total.

In [10]:
# Calculate strike rate for the top 10 run scorers

top_batters = batter_summary["striker"]

top_batter_data = df[df["striker"].isin(top_batters)].copy()

strike_rate_summary = (
    top_batter_data.groupby("striker")
    .agg(
        runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        balls_faced=("wide", lambda x: (x == 0).sum())
    )
    .reset_index()
)

strike_rate_summary["strike_rate"] = (
    strike_rate_summary["runs"] /
    strike_rate_summary["balls_faced"] * 100
)

strike_rate_summary = strike_rate_summary.sort_values(
    "strike_rate", ascending=True
)

plt.figure(figsize=(11, 7))

bars = plt.barh(
    strike_rate_summary["striker"],
    strike_rate_summary["strike_rate"],
    color=IPL_BLUE,
    edgecolor="white"
)

# Highlight the highest strike rate
bars[-1].set_color(TROPHY_GOLD)

plt.title(
    "Strike Rate of the Top 10 Run Scorers — IPL 2026",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Strike Rate", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Batter", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

display(
    strike_rate_summary.sort_values(
        "strike_rate", ascending=False
    ).round(2)
)

Step 11: Runs vs Strike Rate¶

A scatter plot helps us examine the relationship between two numerical variables.

We will:

  • Plot total runs on the X-axis.
  • Plot strike rate on the Y-axis.
  • Label each point with the batter's name.
  • Highlight the batter with the highest run total using the IPL gold color.

This chart helps us identify batters who combine high run volume with fast scoring.

In [11]:
# Compare runs and strike rate for the top 10 batters

scatter_data = strike_rate_summary.copy()

# Identify the highest run scorer
top_scorer = scatter_data.loc[
    scatter_data["runs"].idxmax()
]

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

for _, row in scatter_data.iterrows():
    point_color = (
        TROPHY_GOLD
        if row["striker"] == top_scorer["striker"]
        else IPL_BLUE
    )

    plt.scatter(
        row["runs"],
        row["strike_rate"],
        color=point_color,
        s=130,
        edgecolor="white",
        linewidth=1.2,
        zorder=3
    )

    plt.annotate(
        row["striker"],
        (row["runs"], row["strike_rate"]),
        xytext=(6, 6),
        textcoords="offset points",
        fontsize=9
    )

plt.title(
    "Runs vs Strike Rate — Top 10 Run Scorers",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Total Runs", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Strike Rate", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Step 12: Boundary Analysis of Top 10 Batters¶

Boundaries are an important part of a batter's scoring profile. Comparing fours and sixes helps us understand how different players accumulate runs.

In this step, we will:

  • Count fours (4 runs off the bat) and sixes (6 runs off the bat).
  • Calculate boundary runs for each of the top 10 run scorers.
  • Visualize fours and sixes with a grouped bar chart.
  • Compare players' boundary-scoring patterns.

This analysis focuses on boundaries hit, not total runs scored.

In [12]:
# Boundary analysis for the top 10 run scorers

top_batter_deliveries = df[
    df["striker"].isin(top_batters)
].copy()

boundary_summary = (
    top_batter_deliveries.groupby("striker")
    .agg(
        fours=("runs_of_bat", lambda x: (x == 4).sum()),
        sixes=("runs_of_bat", lambda x: (x == 6).sum())
    )
    .reset_index()
)

boundary_summary["boundary_runs"] = (
    boundary_summary["fours"] * 4 +
    boundary_summary["sixes"] * 6
)

boundary_summary = boundary_summary.sort_values(
    "boundary_runs", ascending=False
)

# Plot grouped bars
x = range(len(boundary_summary))
width = 0.38

plt.figure(figsize=(13, 7))

plt.bar(
    [i - width / 2 for i in x],
    boundary_summary["fours"],
    width=width,
    label="Fours",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)

plt.bar(
    [i + width / 2 for i in x],
    boundary_summary["sixes"],
    width=width,
    label="Sixes",
    color=TROPHY_GOLD
)

Step 13: Boundary Run Contribution¶

Boundary run contribution measures the percentage of a batter's total runs that came from fours and sixes.

Formula:

Boundary Contribution (%) = (Boundary Runs ÷ Total Runs) × 100

In this step, we will:

  • Combine the boundary summary with the total-runs summary.
  • Calculate boundary contribution as a percentage.
  • Visualize the top 10 batters in descending order.
  • Compare the relative importance of boundaries in their scoring.
In [13]:
# Calculate boundary contribution percentage

boundary_contribution = boundary_summary.merge(
    batter_summary[["striker", "total_runs"]],
    on="striker",
    how="left"
)

boundary_contribution["boundary_percentage"] = (
    boundary_contribution["boundary_runs"] /
    boundary_contribution["total_runs"] * 100
)

boundary_contribution = boundary_contribution.sort_values(
    "boundary_percentage"
)

plt.figure(figsize=(11, 7))

bars = plt.barh(
    boundary_contribution["striker"],
    boundary_contribution["boundary_percentage"],
    color=IPL_BLUE,
    edgecolor="white"
)

# Highlight the highest boundary contribution
bars[-1].set_color(TROPHY_GOLD)

plt.title(
    "Boundary Run Contribution — Top 10 Batters",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Boundary Runs (% of Total Runs)", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Batter", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

display(
    boundary_contribution[
        ["striker", "total_runs", "boundary_runs", "boundary_percentage"]

Step 14: Team-Wise Total Runs¶

Team-level aggregation helps us compare how many runs each team scored across its recorded innings.

In this step, we will:

  • Group delivery records by batting team.
  • Calculate total runs scored, including extras.
  • Count the number of recorded innings for each team.
  • Visualize total runs by team.

Since teams may have played different numbers of innings, we will also calculate average runs per recorded innings to provide additional context.

In [14]:
# Calculate team-wise scoring summary

team_summary = (
    df.groupby("batting_team")
    .agg(
        runs_off_bat=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        extras=("extras", "sum"),
        innings_recorded=("match_no", lambda x: df.loc[x.index, ["match_no", "innings"]].drop_duplicates().shape[0])
    )
    .reset_index()
)

team_summary["total_runs"] = (
    team_summary["runs_off_bat"] + team_summary["extras"]
)

team_summary["average_runs_per_innings"] = (
    team_summary["total_runs"] / team_summary["innings_recorded"]
)

team_summary = team_summary.sort_values(
    "total_runs", ascending=True
)

# Plot team-wise total runs
plt.figure(figsize=(11, 7))

bars = plt.barh(
    team_summary["batting_team"],
    team_summary["total_runs"],
    color=IPL_BLUE,
    edgecolor="white"
)

bars[-1].set_color(TROPHY_GOLD)

plt.title(
    "Total Runs Scored by Each Team — IPL 2026",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Total Runs", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Team", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Step 15: Average Runs per Recorded Innings by Team¶

Total runs are influenced by the number of innings recorded for each team. Average runs per innings provides additional context by dividing total runs by the number of recorded innings.

In this step, we will:

  • Sort teams by average runs per recorded innings.
  • Create a horizontal bar chart.
  • Highlight the team with the highest average.
  • Display the number of recorded innings in the labels.

This metric describes the dataset's recorded innings. It is not necessarily the same as an average across completed regulation innings because Super Overs may be included.

Step 16: Team-Wise Innings Score Distribution¶

A team's average score does not show how consistently it scores across innings.

A box plot summarizes:

  • Median: the middle innings score.
  • Interquartile range (IQR): the middle 50% of scores.
  • Whiskers and outliers: the spread of scores and unusually distant values under the box-plot rule.

We will group delivery-level data by match, innings, and batting team to calculate one score per recorded innings. Then we will visualize the score distributions for each team.

Note: The plot describes recorded innings, including any incomplete or Super Over innings present in the data.

In [16]:
# Calculate one total score per recorded innings

innings_scores = (
    df.groupby(["match_no", "innings", "batting_team"], as_index=False)
    .agg(
        innings_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        extras=("extras", "sum")
    )
)

innings_scores["total_score"] = (
    innings_scores["innings_runs"] + innings_scores["extras"]
)

# Order teams by median innings score
team_order = (
    innings_scores.groupby("batting_team")["total_score"]
    .median()
    .sort_values(ascending=False)
    .index
)

# Create team-wise box plot
plt.figure(figsize=(13, 7))

sns.boxplot(
    data=innings_scores,
    x="batting_team",
    y="total_score",
    order=team_order,
    color=IPL_BLUE,
    medianprops={"color": TROPHY_GOLD, "linewidth": 2},
    flierprops={
        "marker": "o",
        "markerfacecolor": TROPHY_GOLD,
        "markeredgecolor": IPL_BLUE,
        "markersize": 5
    }
)

plt.title(
    "Team-Wise Innings Score Distribution — IPL 2026",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Team", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Runs per Recorded Innings", fontsize=12)
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

    .agg(
        innings="count",
        mean="mean",
        median="median",
        minimum="min",
        maximum="max"

Step 17: Scoring Rate Across Match Phases¶

A run rate measures how quickly a team scores. Comparing run rates across match phases helps identify when scoring accelerates or slows down.

We will use these over ranges:

  • Powerplay: overs 1–6
  • Middle overs: overs 7–15
  • Death overs: overs 16–20

For each phase, we will calculate total runs, legal balls, wickets, and run rate.

Formula:

Run Rate = (Total Runs ÷ Legal Balls) × 6

The analysis uses the over number's integer part to assign each delivery to a phase. Wickets are counted from records with a non-null player_dismissed field.

In [17]:
# Step 17: Calculate scoring metrics by match phase

phase_df = df.copy()

# Extract the integer over number from the over.ball notation
phase_df["over_number"] = np.floor(phase_df["over"]).astype(int)

# Assign each delivery to a match phase
phase_df["phase"] = np.select(
    [
        phase_df["over_number"].between(0, 5),
        phase_df["over_number"].between(6, 14),
        phase_df["over_number"].between(15, 19)
    ],
    [
        "Powerplay",
        "Middle Overs",
        "Death Overs"
    ],
    default="Beyond 20 Overs"
)

# Legal delivery: exclude wides and no-balls
phase_df["legal_ball"] = (
    (phase_df["wide"] == 0) &
    (phase_df["noballs"] == 0)
)

# Aggregate phase-level metrics
phase_summary = (
    phase_df.groupby("phase")
    .agg(
        total_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"),
        extras=("extras", "sum"),
        legal_balls=("legal_ball", "sum"),
        wickets=("player_dismissed", "count")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

phase_summary["total_runs"] += phase_summary["extras"]

phase_summary["run_rate"] = (
    phase_summary["total_runs"] /
    phase_summary["legal_balls"] * 6
)

# Keep the intended phase order and exclude empty phases
phase_order = ["Powerplay", "Middle Overs", "Death Overs"]

phase_summary = (
    phase_summary[phase_summary["phase"].isin(phase_order)]
    .set_index("phase")
    .reindex(phase_order)
    .reset_index()
)

# Plot run rate by phase
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

bars = plt.bar(
    phase_summary["phase"],
    phase_summary["run_rate"],
    color=[IPL_BLUE, IPL_BLUE, TROPHY_GOLD],
    edgecolor="white",
    width=0.6
)

for bar, value in zip(bars, phase_summary["run_rate"]):
    plt.text(
        bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2,
        bar.get_height() + 0.1,
        f"{value:.2f}",
        ha="center",
        va="bottom",
        fontweight="bold",
        color=IPL_BLUE
    )

plt.title(
    "Scoring Rate Across Match Phases — IPL 2026",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Match Phase", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Runs per Over", fontsize=12)
plt.ylim(0, phase_summary["run_rate"].max() * 1.15)
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

display(phase_summary.round(2))

Step 18: Wicket Frequency Across Match Phases¶

Raw wicket counts can be misleading because the middle overs cover more overs than the powerplay or death overs.

To compare phases more fairly, we will calculate:

Wicket Rate = (Wickets ÷ Legal Balls) × 100

This metric estimates how many wickets were recorded per 100 legal deliveries in each phase.

We will:

  • Reuse the phase summary from Step 17.
  • Calculate wickets per 100 legal balls.
  • Visualize the wicket rate across the three phases.
  • Compare wicket frequency with the scoring rates from the previous chart.
In [18]:
# Step 18: Calculate wicket rate across match phases

phase_summary["wickets_per_100_balls"] = (
    phase_summary["wickets"] /
    phase_summary["legal_balls"] * 100
)

# Plot wicket rate by phase
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

bars = plt.bar(
    phase_summary["phase"],
    phase_summary["wickets_per_100_balls"],
    color=[IPL_BLUE, IPL_BLUE, TROPHY_GOLD],
    edgecolor="white",
    width=0.6
)

# Add value labels
for bar, value in zip(bars, phase_summary["wickets_per_100_balls"]):
    plt.text(
        bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2,
        bar.get_height() + 0.05,
        f"{value:.2f}",
        ha="center",
        va="bottom",
        fontweight="bold",
        color=IPL_BLUE
    )

plt.title(
    "Wicket Rate Across Match Phases — IPL 2026",
    fontsize=15,
    fontweight="bold",
    color=IPL_BLUE
)
plt.xlabel("Match Phase", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Wickets per 100 Legal Balls", fontsize=12)
plt.ylim(0, phase_summary["wickets_per_100_balls"].max() * 1.2)
plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Step 19: Top 10 Wicket-Taking Bowlers¶

Wicket counts help us compare bowlers' contributions to dismissing batters.

In this step, we will:

  • Include only bowler-credited dismissal types: caught, bowled, lbw, stumped, and hit wicket.
  • Group those dismissals by bowler.
  • Identify the top 10 wicket-takers.
  • Visualize their wicket counts using the IPL color theme.

Note: This chart compares total credited wickets, not bowling efficiency. Bowlers may have bowled different numbers of overs.

In [19]:
# Step 19: Calculate top 10 wicket-taking bowlers

credited_wicket_types = [
    "caught",
    "bowled",
    "lbw",
    "stumped",
    "hit wicket"
]

credited_dismissals = df[
    df["wicket_type"]
    .astype("string")
    .str.strip()
    .str.lower()
    .isin(credited_wicket_types)
].copy()

bowler_wickets = (
    credited_dismissals.groupby("bowler")
    .size()
    .reset_index(name="wickets")
    .sort_values("wickets", ascending=False)
)

top_10_bowlers = bowler_wickets.head(10).sort_values(
    "wickets",
    ascending=True
).reset_index(drop=True)

# Plot top 10 wicket-takers

bars = plt.barh(

)

bars[-1].set_color(TROPHY_GOLD)

# Add wicket-count labels

Step 21: Team-Wise Bowling Performance¶

This visualization compares the bowling performance of IPL 2026 teams using wickets taken and economy rate.

Metrics:

  • X-axis: Total wickets taken by each team
  • Y-axis: Economy rate (runs conceded per over)
  • Each point: One team

Analysis objectives:

  • Calculate total credited wickets for each bowling team.
  • Calculate total runs conceded and legal balls bowled.
  • Calculate each team's economy rate.
  • Visualize the relationship between wicket-taking and economy rate.

The scatter plot helps explore differences in team bowling output and run prevention.

Note: The analysis uses recorded deliveries, including any incomplete innings or Super Overs in the dataset.

In [26]:
# Step 21.1: Calculate team-wise bowling performance

# Work with a copy of the integrated dataset
team_bowling = df.copy()

# Runs conceded by the bowling team
# Includes batter runs, wides, and no-balls
team_bowling["runs_conceded"] = (
    team_bowling["runs_of_bat"]
    + team_bowling["wide"].fillna(0)
    + team_bowling["noballs"].fillna(0)
)

# Legal deliveries exclude wides and no-balls
team_bowling["legal_ball"] = (
    (team_bowling["wide"].fillna(0) == 0)
    & (team_bowling["noballs"].fillna(0) == 0)
).astype(int)

# Wickets credited to the bowler
credited_wicket_types = [
    "caught",
    "bowled",
    "lbw",
    "stumped",
    "hit wicket"
]

team_bowling["credited_wicket"] = (
    team_bowling["wicket_type"]
    .astype("string")
    .str.strip()
    .str.lower()
    .isin(credited_wicket_types)
    .astype(int)
)

# Aggregate metrics by bowling team
team_bowling_summary = (
    team_bowling.groupby("bowling_team")
    .agg(
        total_wickets=("credited_wicket", "sum"),
        total_runs_conceded=("runs_conceded", "sum"),
        legal_balls=("legal_ball", "sum")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Calculate economy rate
team_bowling_summary["economy"] = (
    team_bowling_summary["total_runs_conceded"]
    / (team_bowling_summary["legal_balls"] / 6)
)

# Sort by wickets taken
team_bowling_summary = team_bowling_summary.sort_values(
    "total_wickets",
    ascending=False
).reset_index(drop=True)

display(team_bowling_summary.round(2))

Key Insight:

GT recorded the highest number of credited wickets (118), while KKR had the lowest economy rate (9.04). PBKS recorded the highest economy rate (10.32). These results show that wicket totals and economy rates capture different aspects of team bowling performance.

Step 22: Team-Wise Batting Performance¶

Objective: Compare the batting performance of all teams using total runs scored and run rate.

Metrics:

  • Total Runs: Total runs scored by each batting team.
  • Legal Balls: Deliveries counted as legal balls faced.
  • Run Rate: Average runs scored per over, calculated as:

[ \text{Run Rate} = \frac{\text{Total Runs}}{\text{Legal Balls}} \times 6 ]

Visualization: A scatter plot comparing total runs scored with run rate for each team.

In [30]:
# Calculate team-wise batting performance

team_batting = (
    df.groupby("batting_team")
    .apply(
        lambda group: pd.Series({
            "total_runs": group["runs_of_bat"].sum() + group["extras"].sum(),
            "legal_balls": (
                (group["wide"] == 0) & (group["noballs"] == 0)
            ).sum()
        }),
        include_groups=False
    )
)

team_batting["run_rate"] = (
    team_batting["total_runs"] / team_batting["legal_balls"] * 6
)

team_batting = team_batting.sort_values(
    by="total_runs", ascending=False
).round(2)

Step 24: Toss Decision Analysis¶

Objective: Analyze toss decisions and compare match outcomes based on whether the toss-winning team chose to bat or bowl.

Metrics:

  • Toss Decision Count: Number of matches where the toss winner chose to bat or bowl.
  • Toss Winner Match Wins: Number of matches won by the toss-winning team.
  • Win Percentage: Percentage of matches in which the toss winner also won the match.

Visualization: Bar charts comparing toss decisions and toss-winner match outcomes.

In [37]:
# Prepare one row per match with toss information

toss_data = (
    df[[
        "match_id",
        "toss_winner",
        "toss_decision",
        "match_winner"
    ]]
    .drop_duplicates(subset="match_id")
    .dropna(subset=["toss_winner", "toss_decision", "match_winner"])
    .copy()
)

# Check toss decision counts
toss_counts = toss_data["toss_decision"].value_counts()

# Check whether the toss winner also won the match
toss_data["toss_winner_won"] = (
    toss_data["toss_winner"] == toss_data["match_winner"]
)

toss_outcomes = (
    toss_data.groupby("toss_decision")
    .agg(
        total_matches=("match_id", "count"),
        toss_winner_wins=("toss_winner_won", "sum")
    )
)

toss_outcomes["win_percentage"] = (
    toss_outcomes["toss_winner_wins"]
    / toss_outcomes["total_matches"] * 100
).round(2)

display(toss_counts)
display(toss_outcomes)

Calculate winning margins¶

In [42]:
# Prepare one row per match

match_data = (
    df[[
        "match_id",
        "match_winner",
        "first_ings_score",
        "second_ings_score",
        "first_ings_wkts",
        "second_ings_wkts",
        "match_result"
    ]]
    .drop_duplicates(subset="match_id")
    .copy()
)

# Keep completed matches with recorded winners
completed = match_data[
    (match_data["match_result"] == "completed") &
    (match_data["match_winner"].notna())
].copy()

# Calculate winning type and margin
def get_margin(row):
    if row["second_ings_score"] > row["first_ings_score"]:
        return pd.Series({
            "win_type": "Wickets",
            "winning_margin": 10 - row["second_ings_wkts"]
        })
    elif row["first_ings_score"] > row["second_ings_score"]:
        return pd.Series({
            "win_type": "Runs",
            "winning_margin": (
                row["first_ings_score"] - row["second_ings_score"]
            )
        })
    else:
        return pd.Series({
            "win_type": "Needs review",
            "winning_margin": None
        })

completed[["win_type", "winning_margin"]] = completed.apply(
    get_margin, axis=1
)

display(
    completed[
        ["match_id", "match_winner", "win_type", "winning_margin"]
    ].head(10)
)

print("\nWin type counts:")
display(completed["win_type"].value_counts())

batter_summary = (
    df.groupby("striker")
    .agg(total_runs=("runs_of_bat", "sum"))
    .reset_index()
)

balls_faced = (
    df.assign(valid_ball=(df["wide"].fillna(0) == 0))
    .groupby("striker")["valid_ball"]
    .sum()
    .reset_index(name="balls_faced")
)

batter_summary = batter_summary.merge(
    balls_faced,
    on="striker",
    how="left"
)

batter_summary["strike_rate"] = (
    batter_summary["total_runs"]
    / batter_summary["balls_faced"].replace(0, float("nan"))
    * 100
).round(2)

print("Total batters:", len(batter_summary))

Calculate strike rate accurately¶

In [61]:
# Count balls faced, excluding wides
balls_faced = (
    df.assign(valid_ball=(df["wide"].fillna(0) == 0))
    .groupby("striker")["valid_ball"]
    .sum()
    .reset_index(name="balls_faced")
)

batter_summary = batter_summary.drop(
    columns=["strike_rate", "balls_recorded"],
    errors="ignore"
).merge(balls_faced, on="striker", how="left")

batter_summary["strike_rate"] = (
    batter_summary["total_runs"] /
    batter_summary["balls_faced"].replace(0, float("nan")) * 100
).round(2)

print("Total batters:", len(batter_summary))
display(batter_summary.nlargest(10, "total_runs"))

Step 31: Batter Performance — Runs vs. Balls Faced¶

Objective: Analyze the relationship between balls faced and total runs scored by batters across the available IPL 2026 data.

Chart: Scatter plot

  • X-axis: Balls Faced
  • Y-axis: Total Runs
  • Each point represents one batter.
In [64]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

plt.scatter(
    batter_summary["balls_faced"],
    batter_summary["total_runs"],
    color="#1E3A8A",
    alpha=0.65,
    s=65
)

plt.title(
    "Batter Performance: Runs vs. Balls Faced — IPL 2026",
    fontsize=14,
    fontweight="bold"
)
plt.xlabel("Balls Faced")
plt.ylabel("Total Runs")
plt.grid(True, linestyle="--", alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Key Insights:

  • The scatter plot shows a clear positive relationship between balls faced and total runs scored.
  • Most batters are concentrated in the lower-left region, indicating fewer balls faced and lower run totals.
  • A few batters stand out with high run totals after facing more than 300 balls.
  • Batters facing a similar number of balls can still score different totals, reflecting

from pathlib import Path
import json
import base64

# Find the notebook file
candidates = [
    Path("04_data_visualization.ipynb"),
    Path("notebooks/04_data_visualization.ipynb")
]

notebook_path = next(
    (path for path in candidates if path.exists()),
    None
)

if notebook_path is None:
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not find 04_data_visualization.ipynb")

# Create the Visualizations folder in the project root
if notebook_path.parent == Path("."):
    output_dir = Path("../Visualizations")
else:
    output_dir = notebook_path.parent.parent / "Visualizations"

output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Read the saved notebook
with open(notebook_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    notebook = json.load(file)

chart_count = 0

# Extract every embedded PNG chart
for cell_number, cell in enumerate(notebook["cells"], start=1):
    for output in cell.get("outputs", []):
        image_data = output.get("data", {}).get("image/png")

        if image_data:
            if isinstance(image_data, list):
                image_data = "".join(image_data)

            chart_count += 1
            filename = f"chart_{chart_count:02d}.png"

            image_bytes = base64.b64decode(image_data)

            with open(output_dir / filename, "wb") as image_file:
                image_file.write(image_bytes)

print(f"Successfully saved {chart_count} charts!")
print(f"Folder location: {output_dir.resolve()}")
